intelligence.enrichment: Cyclones are large storms that form over warm ocean waters; heated ocean water makes warm moist air rise, the water vapour condenses to raindrops, and the storm develops a lowest-pressure centre called the eye where winds are calm while surrounding regions have strong winds and heavy rainfall. Warm ocean heating leads to rising moist air and condensation; the low-pressure storm draws in surrounding air and can develop into a cyclone with a calm low-pressure eye and destructive surrounding winds and rain. The learner explains cyclone formation over warm ocean water and distinguishes the calm lowest-pressure eye from the surrounding strong winds and heavy rainfall. A cyclone is just a very windy thunderstorm, and the centre must be the most dangerous part because it is the middle.
